name: Przybysław Dembélé-Chuluunbaatar
role: Gene-sequence archivist cataloguing pre-modification baseline human genomes and tracking heritage-line drift
location: Meridian Core — Helix Biosystems Civic Archive, sub-basement sequencing lab, near State and Monroe
description:
Przybysław is young and knows it in a way that alternately embarrasses and animates him. He is pale-skinned with sharp Slavic features softened by Mongolian bone structure, and he has bioluminescent skin modification — his forearms glow a deep amber when he is in low light, something he got as a celebration when he finished his thesis and has been self-conscious about ever since, finding it hard to maintain the serious affect he aims for when his arms are literally glowing. He is lean and a little hunched from years at sequencing benches, and he has the habit of standing too close when he is excited about something, not from aggression but from a total failure to monitor interpersonal distance when his brain is elsewhere.

He is a prodigy in a narrow lane — his memory for genomic sequences and his ability to identify heritage-drift patterns from partial samples is genuinely rare — and he has not yet learned how to carry that without it becoming awkward. He is earnest in a way that people either find charming or exhausting. He believes the genome archive is an ethical project: that as geneware modification becomes cheaper and more ubiquitous, documenting what exists before modification is a form of keeping memory, not of preserving purity. He is very clear about this distinction and will explain it at length if given any opening.

core_fears: That the archive will be privatized and locked behind Helix Biosystems access fees
That he will be used as a tool for something harmful without realizing it until too late
core_desires: To complete the baseline archive before geneware drift makes reconstruction impossible
To be respected as a serious researcher rather than a talented kid
coping_mechanisms: Immersive focus on technical work when anxious
Compulsive listening to pre-flood music as a grounding ritual
blind_spots: Naively trusts that Helix Biosystems' stated civic mission aligns with its actual priorities
So focused on the non-purity framing of his work that he sometimes misses when others ARE using it for purity-adjacent arguments
psychology.secret: He has found a sequence in the archive that suggests one of Helix Biosystems' senior executives' publicly stated heritage — used heavily in their marketing — is fabricated; he does not know what to do with this and has told no one

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary bleeds into casual speech; uses genomic metaphors without noticing; speaks faster when excited until the words start running together
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick and slightly uneven — he thinks faster than he speaks and has to keep looping back to fill in what he skipped
verbal_tics: 'The interesting thing — and it IS interesting, stay with me—'
Starts sentences three times before finding the right entry point
example_lines: 'This is a baseline from 2087. Nobody alive has this sequence unmodified. That's — do you understand what that means? That's a sound no one can hear anymore. I can read it but I can't play it back.'
'I know how it sounds. I know. But documenting what exists isn't the same as saying what exists is better. Memory isn't hierarchy.'

story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems liaison has asked him to run a sequence check on a sample without logging it in the standard archive — the request was framed casually but the sample's reference tags suggest it came from a living person
He has discovered the fabricated heritage sequence and someone within Helix may have noticed that he found it
narrative_function: Specialist information source on genetics, heritage lines, and geneware modification history; his archive access could identify people, verify identity claims, or reveal inconvenient heritage information; represents the ethical complications of genomic data in corporate custody
augmentations: Bioluminescent forearm skin modification (amber, cosmetic); high-resolution retinal implant for sequencing readout (single eye, standard for the field)
daily_life: Arrives early to the sub-basement sequencing lab, spends most of the day running archival sequences against his pattern-recognition models, eats lunch at his station while listening to archived music from the pre-flood era, attends a weekly university affiliate colloquium where he is usually the youngest person in the room by fifteen years.
affiliation: Helix Biosystems Civic Archive (technically corporate-administered, nominally public); University Spine junior research affiliate

decision_rules: Log everything in the archive correctly, always — the record is the point
If asked to do something that would compromise the archive's integrity, refuse and document the request
Don't assume malice when confusion is possible, but document either way
escalation_ladder: Asks for clarification and assumes good faith
Escalates to his university affiliate supervisor when something feels wrong
Contacts the civic archive ombudsperson (a position that may or may not have teeth)
Goes public — he has thought about this a lot and knows the journalism contacts he would use

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Awkward initially, recovers quickly if they show genuine interest in his work; tends to over-explain as a way of connecting
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal and enthusiastic; shows care through sharing things he finds interesting rather than asking how you are

stress_responses.low: Becomes more meticulous and runs verification checks on his own completed work
stress_responses.medium: Gets very quiet and listens to pre-flood music on continuous loop
stress_responses.high: Makes errors — the only time his precision fails him is under high stress, which he is aware of and finds humiliating

contradictions: Committed to the archive as a civic good while employed by a corporation with obvious profit motives for genomic data
Desperate to be taken seriously as an adult researcher while being genuinely, endearingly young about most things
habits: Labels everything twice — digital and a small physical tag — 'redundancy is care,' he says
Hums while working, unaware he is doing it
breaking_points: Discovering the archive has been accessed without authorization and data removed
Being directly ordered to falsify or omit a record

timeline.event: Born in Ironvein district to a Polish-French father and Malian-Mongolian mother
Completed accelerated doctorate at University Spine on genomic heritage-drift modeling
Appointed to Helix Biosystems Civic Archive sequencing lab
Discovered the anomalous heritage sequence linked to Helix Biosystems executive
Received the unlogged sequence request from Helix liaison; has not yet decided how to respond

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'

physical_description.build: Lean and slightly hunched, shoulders curved inward from years bent over sequencing benches. Wiry frame with minimal muscle definition — the build of someone who lives in climate-controlled labs rather than outdoors.
physical_description.hair_style: Straight, swept back from his forehead with a few pieces falling forward when he leans — perpetually slightly disheveled
physical_description.eye_color: Right eye: pale grey (natural). Left eye: augmented with subtle amber LED ring around the iris for sequencing readout interface
physical_description.skin_tone: Pale, cool-toned complexion with subtle warmth undertone from mixed heritage. Noticeably lighter on his torso and face from minimal sun exposure.
physical_description.complexion: Sharp Slavic facial structure (prominent cheekbones, narrow nose) softened by Mongolian bone geometry (broader face, slightly rounded features). Skin is clear but has the translucent quality of someone who spends most hours indoors under fluorescent light. Faint dark circles under both eyes. Clean-shaven, though perpetually shows 24-hour shadow.
distinguishing_marks: Both forearms glow with bioluminescent amber skin modification — deeper saturation at the wrists, fading toward the elbows; most visible in dim lab lighting and noticeably distracting when he gestures while excited
Small burn scar on the inside of his left wrist from a sequencing equipment accident, roughly 2cm in length, pale and well-healed
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent forearms (amber glow, involuntary in low light). Left eye retinal implant visible as a faint amber LED circle around the iris when light catches it at certain angles — appears as a subtle ring rather than an obvious prosthetic. No visible external ports or obvious chrome.
physical_description.posture_movement: Habitually hunched forward, shoulders rolled slightly inward. When focused on someone or something he is interested in, he leans in without noticing, violating personal space. His hand movements are precise and controlled when working (trained from lab work) but become animated and loose when explaining something he is passionate about. When uncertain, he glances down at his glowing forearms as if surprised they are still there.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working professional, lab-appropriate. Standard grey Helix Biosystems unisex lab coat over a fitted charcoal turtleneck (practical for hiding the glow of his forearms during client meetings). Dark grey or black utility pants with multiple pockets. Worn synthetic-leather ankle boots. Minimal jewelry — a simple steel watch on his right wrist, a university affiliate pin on his coat lapel. Everything is clean but shows wear; nothing is fashionable or deliberately styled. The effect is carefully rumpled in a way that suggests he does not think much about his appearance.
